name: Finerenone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Finerenone is a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA). The US label sets the starting dose by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and serum potassium, and does not recommend starting it below eGFR 25 mL/min/1.73 m2.

bands.recommendation: Start 20 mg once daily (label). Do not start if serum potassium >5.0 mEq/L. CKD with diabetes: target 20 mg. Heart failure (LVEF ≥40%): target 40 mg.
Start 10 mg once daily (label: eGFR ≥25 to <60). Recheck potassium at 4 weeks; increase to 20 mg if K ≤4.8 mEq/L and eGFR has not fallen >30%. Heart failure target 20 mg.
eGFR 25–29: start 10 mg once daily as above. eGFR <25: initiation not recommended (label).

hd: No data in label. Insufficient data: avoid or use with specialist input.
pd: No data in label. Insufficient data: avoid or use with specialist input.
crrt: No data in label. Insufficient data: avoid.
dialyzable: Unlikely to be removed by hemodialysis (about 90% protein bound; label).
monitoring: Serum potassium and eGFR before starting, 4 weeks after starting or changing dose, and periodically. Withhold if K >5.5 mEq/L; restart at 10 mg when K ≤5.0 mEq/L.

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and efficacy not established below 18 years (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
